BUILDING AN INTELLIGENT MULTI-AGENT BUSINESS EXPERT USING AMAZON BEDROCK Single-model AI systems often struggle when processing complex business decisions that span multiple domains of expertise (R&D, Legal, Finance). Stuffing all contextual data into a single prompt easily leads to context window overload, inflated token costs, and hallucinations.
AWS introduced the Multi-Agent Collaboration solution on Amazon Bedrock. Key architectural components include:
Amazon Bedrock Agents: Building specialized autonomous agents tailored to specific business domains. Supervisor Agent: Orchestrating workflows, delegating sub-tasks, and synthesizing final answers. Knowledge Bases: Connecting research papers, compliance documentation, and patent databases as reference sources. AWS Lambda: Action Groups executing real-time data queries and financial calculations. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails: Enforcing content filtering, privacy boundaries, and sensitive data protection. The system features three specialized sub-agents collaborating with the Supervisor:
R&D Agent: Queries technical specifications, clinical trials, and drug experiment records. Legal Agent: Reviews contracts, IP filings, and regulatory compliance risks. Finance Agent: Analyzes production costs, pricing strategies, and market forecasts. The key strength of this architecture is context isolation — each specialized agent operates strictly within its functional domain, boosting accuracy and slashing token consumption. When expanding operations, organizations simply attach new domain agents without rearchitecting the entire system.
Key Takeaways:
Provide crisp, explicit system instructions for the Supervisor Agent to ensure precise delegation. Domain knowledge bases must be tailored and indexed properly for real-world production data. Inter-agent invocation frequency directly impacts total inference cost. Leverage Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to enforce least-privilege data access across business units. title: Workshop Overview & Architecture
content:
5.1 Workshop Overview & Solution Architecture 1. Real-World Context & Problem Statement As organizations accelerate their migration to cloud infrastructure (Cloud Migration), engineering teams heavily rely on Infrastructure as Code (IaC) – predominantly Terraform (HCL) – to automate continuous provisioning. While IaC accelerates development velocity, it simultaneously introduces widespread security risks when configuration errors (Misconfigurations) are deployed unnoticed.
Industry cybersecurity telemetry reveals:
Over 80% of enterprise cloud data breaches originate from basic human misconfigurations (such as public SSH Port 22 exposure to 0.0.0.0/0, publicly accessible S3 buckets, and unencrypted data volumes). Remediating security vulnerabilities post-deployment in production environments costs up to 30x more than resolving them during the initial authoring phase (the core philosophy of Shift-Left Security). Traditional static application security testing (SAST) tools (e.g., Checkov, tfsec) rely on rigid regex rules, produce excessive False Positives, lack contextual understanding of interconnected cloud resources, and cannot generate automated remediation code for developers. CloudGuard AI solves these limitations by combining the multi-step reasoning capabilities of Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet) with the definitive compliance standards of the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0 through advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
2. Solution Architecture CloudGuard AI is built strictly according to the AWS Well-Architected Framework, operating as a 100% event-driven serverless architecture that ensures continuous high availability, defense-in-depth security, and near-zero idle operating costs.
Below is the official solution architecture diagram:
3. Architecture Layers Breakdown The system is logically structured into 6 decoupled functional layers:
Global Services & Edge Security Layer:
AWS WAF: Enforces managed Web ACL rules blocking DDoS, volumetric scraping, and SQLi/XSS at the AWS network edge. AWS IAM: Enforces least-privilege role-based access control (RBAC) execution roles for AWS Lambda and the Bedrock Agent. Amazon CloudFront: Global CDN delivering low-latency distribution with edge SSL/TLS certificates managed via AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in us-east-1. Amazon Cognito: User Pools authenticating DevOps engineers via cryptographically signed JSON Web Tokens (JWT) protecting API endpoints. API & Configuration Layer:
Amazon API Gateway (HTTP API): High-throughput ingestion entry point for scan requests (POST /scan) and audit history queries (GET /history), equipped with built-in JWT authorizers and rate limiting. AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Parameter Store: Encrypted centralized repository storing operational parameters, Bedrock Knowledge Base IDs, and notification webhooks. AWS ACM (ap-southeast-1): Regional SSL/TLS certificate management for regional API Gateway custom domains. Compute & Scheduling Layer:
AWS Lambda (Core Audit Engine): The primary serverless execution engine running Python 3.12, orchestrating AST parsing of Terraform files, Bedrock RAG querying, posture scoring, and JSON response formatting. AWS Amplify: Full-stack hosting and delivery platform for the modern React/Next.js dashboard where users paste code and inspect visual scorecards. Amazon EventBridge Scheduler: Serverless cron orchestrator invoking Lambda on a recurring daily cadence to assess running infrastructure states. Data & Storage Layer:
Amazon S3: Secure object storage hosting CIS Benchmark v3.0 regulatory PDFs, raw sample Terraform templates, and generated PDF compliance reports. Amazon DynamoDB: Single-digit millisecond latency NoSQL database storing audit sessions, posture scores, and granular finding records. Amazon SES: Automated transactional email engine delivering scheduled audit summaries and executive posture reports. GenAI & RAG Brain Layer:
Amazon Bedrock Agent: Intelligent reasoning agent powered by Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet, conducting multi-step logical deduction, resource correlation, and precise Terraform code remediation. Bedrock Knowledge Bases (RAG): Uses Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 coupled with a high-performance vector store to ingest, chunk, and semantically retrieve relevant CIS Benchmark sections. Bedrock Guardrails: AI safety perimeter preventing prompt injection attacks, enforcing responsible AI boundaries, and masking credentials (AWS keys, passwords, JWTs) and Personally Identifiable Information (PII). Monitoring & Alerting Layer:
Amazon CloudWatch: Centralized observability platform collecting Lambda execution logs, Bedrock token consumption, and operational health metrics. Amazon SNS: Real-time pub/sub notification service dispatching immediate critical alerts to administrator channels (Slack, SMS, Email) upon detecting CRITICAL severity vulnerabilities. 4. End-to-End Operational Lifecycle [Developer / CI-CD] --(1. Send Terraform code)--> [API Gateway / CloudFront] | (2. Trigger Lambda Invoke) v [AWS Lambda Core Engine] | | (3. Query CIS rules via RAG) | | (5. Save history) v v [Bedrock RAG Engine] [DynamoDB Table] | | (4. Claude 3.5 Sonnet Reasoning) | (6. Alert if CRITICAL) v v [Auto-Fix Code & Score] [Amazon SNS / Email] Step 1 (Submission): Developers paste Terraform code into the web UI or external CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions) dispatch a webhook payload to API Gateway (POST /scan). Step 2 (Decomposition): The Lambda Core Engine parses the HCL syntax to isolate security-sensitive resource definitions (Security Group rules, S3 bucket encryption, IAM policies). Step 3 (RAG Retrieval): Lambda constructs a semantic search query against the Bedrock Knowledge Base to retrieve governing CIS Benchmark clauses. Step 4 (AI Reasoning & Auto-Fix): Claude 3.5 Sonnet evaluates the code against retrieved standards, assigns severity levels (CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW), computes an aggregate compliance score (0-100), and synthesizes remediated Terraform code. Step 5 (Persistence & Escalation): Findings are persisted in DynamoDB; if the score is below 70 or CRITICAL flaws are discovered, an emergency SNS notification is dispatched. 5. Workshop Specifications Estimated Duration: ~90 minutes Difficulty Level: Intermediate Recommended AWS Regions: ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) or us-east-1 (N. Virginia) Estimated Cost: $0.00 USD (Fully compliant with the AWS Free Tier and Bedrock trial allocations).

title: Prerequisites & IAM Configuration
content:
5.2 Prerequisites & IAM Configuration Before constructing the core components of CloudGuard AI, you must prepare your AWS account environment, activate Foundation Model access in Amazon Bedrock, and provision supporting serverless resources (Amazon S3, DynamoDB, and IAM Roles).
Step 1: Verify AWS Account & Configure AWS CLI You can complete this lab directly using AWS CloudShell (the integrated browser-based shell on the AWS Management Console) or via a local terminal configured with AWS CLI v2.
Verify your authenticated AWS identity: aws sts get-caller-identity Expected output:
{ "UserId": "AIDASAMPLEUSERIDEXAMPLE", "Account": "123456789012", "Arn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/devops-admin" } Note your 12-digit AWS Account ID (e.g., 123456789012), as it is required to formulate globally unique S3 bucket names.
Export environment variables for the deployment region (prefer ap-southeast-1 Singapore or us-east-1 N. Virginia for comprehensive Bedrock model availability):
export AWS_REGION="ap-southeast-1" export AWS_ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text) Step 2: Request Foundation Model Access in Amazon Bedrock Amazon Bedrock enforces an explicit opt-in model before API access is granted for foundation models.
Navigate to the AWS Management Console and select Amazon Bedrock. In the left navigation pane, scroll to Bedrock configurations and click Model access. Select Modify model access (or Enable specific models). Check the following two essential models: Anthropic: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (or Claude 3 Sonnet). Amazon: Titan Text Embeddings V2. Click Next, review and accept the End User License Agreements (EULA), then click Submit. Wait 1-2 minutes until the Access status for both models displays green: Access granted. Step 3: Create Amazon S3 Bucket for CIS Benchmark Knowledge Assets Amazon S3 acts as the authoritative Data Source container for the Bedrock Knowledge Base.
Create a new globally unique S3 bucket: aws s3 mb s3://cloudguard-audit-data-${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID} --region ${AWS_REGION} Enable Block Public Access to guarantee complete data confidentiality: aws s3api put-public-access-block \ --bucket cloudguard-audit-data-${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID} \ --public-access-block-configuration "BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true" Enable default Server-Side Encryption (SSE-S3): aws s3api put-bucket-encryption \ --bucket cloudguard-audit-data-${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID} \ --server-side-encryption-configuration '{"Rules": [{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {"SSEAlgorithm": "AES256"}}]}' Create the knowledge-base/ prefix inside the bucket to organize CIS Benchmark rule files: aws s3api put-object --bucket cloudguard-audit-data-${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID} --key knowledge-base/ Step 4: Create Amazon DynamoDB Table for Audit Histories The platform persists all audit findings (timestamp, compliance posture score, identified vulnerabilities, and remediated code). We use Amazon DynamoDB in On-Demand (Pay-Per-Request) mode to incur zero idle cost.
Provision the CloudGuard_ScanHistory table with scan_id as the Partition Key: aws dynamodb create-table \ --table-name CloudGuard_ScanHistory \ --attribute-definitions AttributeName=scan_id,AttributeType=S \ --key-schema AttributeName=scan_id,KeyType=HASH \ --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST \ --region ${AWS_REGION} Verify that the table status transitions to ACTIVE: aws dynamodb describe-table \ --table-name CloudGuard_ScanHistory \ --query "Table.TableStatus" \ --output text Step 5: Provision IAM Execution Role for AWS Lambda The Lambda Core Audit Engine requires least-privilege permissions to query Bedrock RAG, access S3 objects, read/write DynamoDB records, and stream CloudWatch Logs.
Create the trust policy document allowing Lambda execution (lambda-trust-policy.json): { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "Service": "lambda.amazonaws.com" }, "Action": "sts:AssumeRole" } ] } Create the IAM Role CloudGuard_Lambda_ExecutionRole: aws iam create-role \ --role-name CloudGuard_Lambda_ExecutionRole \ --assume-role-policy-document file://lambda-trust-policy.json Define the granular inline permissions policy (lambda-permissions-policy.json): { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "BedrockInvokePermissions", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": [ "bedrock:InvokeModel", "bedrock:Retrieve", "bedrock:RetrieveAndGenerate" ], "Resource": "*" }, { "Sid": "S3BucketAccess", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": [ "s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject", "s3:ListBucket" ], "Resource": [ "arn:aws:s3:::cloudguard-audit-data-*", "arn:aws:s3:::cloudguard-audit-data-*/*" ] }, { "Sid": "DynamoDBReadWrite", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": [ "dynamodb:PutItem", "dynamodb:GetItem", "dynamodb:Query", "dynamodb:Scan" ], "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:*:*:table/CloudGuard_ScanHistory" }, { "Sid": "CloudWatchLogs", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": [ "logs:CreateLogGroup", "logs:CreateLogStream", "logs:PutLogEvents" ], "Resource": "arn:aws:logs:*:*:*" }, { "Sid": "SNSPublish", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": [ "sns:Publish" ], "Resource": "*" } ] } Attach the policy to the newly created role: aws iam put-role-policy \ --role-name CloudGuard_Lambda_ExecutionRole \ --policy-name CloudGuard_Core_Policy \ --policy-document file://lambda-permissions-policy.json With initial environment prerequisites and IAM security boundaries established, we are ready to proceed to Building the Bedrock Knowledge Base with CIS Benchmark v3.0!

title: Proposal
content:
CloudGuard AI: Automated AWS Infrastructure Security & Cost Auditor GenAI & RAG-Powered Automated Security Compliance (CIS Benchmark v3.0) and Cloud Cost Optimization 1. Executive Summary This project builds a complete cloud infrastructure security auditing and cost optimization platform (DevSecOps & FinOps), consisting of two decoupled applications: Backend — a serverless REST API built with Python 3.12 on AWS Lambda + API Gateway, orchestrating Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) via Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 to parse Terraform HCL Abstract Syntax Trees (AST), cross-reference the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, calculate compliance posture scores (0–100), and generate automated remediation code — and Frontend — a Next.js SSR application built on React, featuring a bilingual vi/en UI, dark/light themes, a visual Security Gauge, severity-tagged finding accordions, and a side-by-side diff viewer with a one-click code copy action.
The goal of this workshop is to deploy the entire system onto AWS Serverless infrastructure (region ap-southeast-1): the Next.js SSR frontend runs on AWS Amplify, the Python core engine runs on Lambda + API Gateway, all behind CloudFront and secured by AWS WAF and Amazon Cognito — demonstrating the ability to apply AWS services to a real, end-to-end use case. Target customers are DevOps/Cloud Engineers requiring automated pre-merge security verification (Shift-Left Security), SecOps compliance officers auditing cloud postures, and FinOps administrators seeking cloud waste reduction.
2. Problem Statement What’s the Problem?
Infrastructure misconfigurations causing widespread data exposure: over 80% of cloud security incidents stem from human configuration errors (SSH port 22 open to 0.0.0.0/0, unencrypted S3 storage, overly permissive wildcard IAM policies). Manual code reviews create release bottlenecks: manual line-by-line inspection takes 2–3 days, delaying sprint delivery. Traditional static analysis linters lack architectural context: regex-based linters (Checkov, tfsec) suffer from high false-positive rates, cannot interpret inter-resource relationships, and cannot rewrite compliant code. Generative AI hallucination risks: general-purpose LLMs hallucinate non-existent compliance clauses or produce deprecated Terraform syntax without grounding. Idle server costs: provisioning dedicated GPU-enabled EC2 instances wastes hundreds of dollars per month during inactive scanning windows. The Solution A serverless, pay-per-request, auto-scaling architecture: Python Core Engine runs on Lambda + API Gateway (HTTP API), Next.js SSR is hosted on AWS Amplify, and CloudFront (with an edge-attached WAF Web ACL) distributes assets and routes API requests. The RAG architecture in Bedrock Knowledge Base (Titan Text Embeddings V2 + Vector DB) anchors reasoning strictly to the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, eliminating hallucinations. Bedrock Agent (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) evaluates contextual risk, computes scores, and generates compliant remediation snippets. CloudWatch Logs/Metrics + Alarm + SNS provide centralized observability and instant admin escalation; WAF, IAM least-privilege, Cognito, and SSM Parameter Store enforce security; EventBridge Scheduler + Lambda handles daily automated posture scans.
Benefits and Return on Investment The platform auto-scales on demand at a monthly operating cost of only ~$11–15/month — the serverless design eliminates 100% of idle costs (Zero Idle Cost), avoiding dedicated EC2/GPU instances and saving >95% compared to static infrastructure. It accelerates review cycles by 90% (from 2–3 days to <10 seconds), eliminates 100% of baseline misconfigurations pre-deployment, and the bilingual step-by-step workshop produced at the end serves as an enduring educational asset for the cloud engineering community.
3. Solution Architecture User requests flow through CloudFront (WAF Web ACL attached at the edge) to two origins: Amplify (Next.js SSR frontend, Static/SSR flow) and API Gateway (HTTP API) → Lambda (Python Core Audit Engine, API Calls flow); Amplify also performs “SSR fetch” calls back to the API during server rendering. DevOps engineers authenticate via Amazon Cognito (JWT Auth). External CI/CD pipelines (GitHub/GitLab PR) dispatch automated webhook scan payloads to API Gateway. Lambda parses Terraform AST, queries CIS Benchmark v3.0 rules via Bedrock Knowledge Bases (RAG), prompts Claude 3.5 Sonnet, reads configuration from SSM Parameter Store, saves PDF summaries in S3 via Pre-signed URLs, writes audit records to DynamoDB, and dispatches email via SES. EventBridge Scheduler triggers a daily Lambda scan. CloudWatch aggregates logs/metrics; on threshold breach or CRITICAL finding, an Alarm publishes to SNS, alerting administrators via email. The architecture is detailed below:
Note on WAF: WAF is not a standalone hop on the network path — the Web ACL is attached directly to the CloudFront distribution and evaluates requests at the edge location before CloudFront processes them. A Web ACL used with CloudFront must be created in the Global scope (us-east-1).
AWS Services Used
AWS Lambda: Runs the Python 3.12 Core Audit Engine + cron jobs — serverless, 1M free requests/month, cold-start optimized. Amazon API Gateway (HTTP API): REST API front door — ~70% cheaper than REST API Gateway, native Lambda integration. AWS Amplify: Next.js SSR hosting with automated Git CI/CD. Amazon CloudFront: CDN serving static assets/SSR and API — global edge locations cut latency, attachment point for WAF Web ACL. Amazon Cognito: User directory management (User Pools) issuing cryptographically signed JWT tokens for DevOps access. Amazon Bedrock Agent: Intelligent reasoning agent powered by Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet for multi-step policy deduction and code remediation. Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases (RAG): Semantic vector search engine indexing CIS Benchmark v3.0 using Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails: Enforces safety guardrails, blocking prompt injections and masking secrets (AWS keys, credentials, PII). Amazon S3: Object storage for CIS Benchmark standards, raw IaC templates, and compiled PDF reports via Pre-signed URLs; public access blocked. Amazon DynamoDB: Low-latency NoSQL database recording scan histories, compliance scores, and granular finding records. Amazon SES: Transactional email engine delivering audit summaries and executive posture reports. Amazon CloudWatch: Logs, metrics, and alarms integrated natively with Lambda and API Gateway. Amazon SNS: Real-time administrative alerting via direct email subscription upon CRITICAL findings. Amazon EventBridge Scheduler: Serverless cron trigger executing daily automated infrastructure compliance scans. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: Encrypted centralized store for application parameters and webhook secrets. IAM + ACM + WAF: Least-privilege roles; free SSL/TLS certificates (ACM in us-east-1 for CloudFront, ACM in ap-southeast-1 for API Gateway); layer-7 attack protection. Component Design
Content delivery & Edge: CloudFront serves static assets/SSR and API at global edge locations; WAF Web ACL filters requests at the edge; Cognito handles JWT authentication. Frontend: AWS Amplify hosts the Next.js 15 SSR application, deployed automatically from Git. Core Audit Processing: AWS Lambda wraps Terraform HCL AST parsing behind API Gateway HTTP API. Generative AI & RAG: Bedrock Knowledge Base vector store + Claude 3.5 Sonnet agent for multi-step reasoning and automated remediation. Data layer: DynamoDB persists audit session records; S3 stores regulatory standards and PDF reports via Pre-signed URLs. Automation & Alerting: EventBridge Scheduler invokes Lambda daily; CloudWatch + SNS broadcast instant critical alerts. Security & Certificates: Lambda Execution Role scoped to Least Privilege; HTTPS-only with ACM certificates; secrets stored in SSM Parameter Store. 4. Technical Implementation Implementation Phases
Research & design: learn AWS fundamentals (IAM, Lambda, Bedrock, S3, API Gateway); study serverless RAG patterns for IaC (Weeks 1–2). Application development & RAG: standardize CIS Benchmark v3.0 rules, build Terraform AST parser, integrate Bedrock RAG (Weeks 3–5). AWS infrastructure deployment: create IAM roles; deploy core engine to Lambda + API Gateway; deploy FE to Amplify; configure S3, DynamoDB, Bedrock Knowledge Base, CloudFront, WAF, SSM Parameter Store (Weeks 6–8). Monitoring & optimization: configure CloudWatch Logs/Metrics, Alarm → SNS, EventBridge cron; optimize Bedrock token consumption (Weeks 9–10). Testing & documentation: end-to-end testing with benchmark violation test suites; write bilingual step-by-step workshop and clean-up guide (Weeks 11–12). Technical Requirements
Backend: Python 3.12 (boto3, bedrock-agent-runtime, regex HCL parser), cold-start optimized, deployed behind API Gateway HTTP API. AI & RAG: Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 (1,024 dimensions), OpenSearch Serverless vector collection, Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Frontend: Next.js (TypeScript, TailwindCSS) built and hosted on AWS Amplify with SSR support. Networking & security: WAF Web ACL in Global scope (us-east-1) attached to CloudFront; ACM certificates in us-east-1 (CloudFront) and ap-southeast-1 (API Gateway); secrets managed in SSM Parameter Store; Cognito JWT auth. 5. Timeline & Milestones Project Timeline (12 weeks)
Phase 1 — Research & design (Weeks 1–2): AWS fundamentals, serverless GenAI & RAG architecture study → deliverable: this proposal + draw.io architecture diagram. Phase 2 — Core Engine & RAG development (Weeks 3–5): CIS Benchmark dataset preparation, Terraform HCL parser, Bedrock RAG integration → deliverable: local prototype running end-to-end. Phase 3 — AWS infrastructure deployment (Weeks 6–8): IAM, Lambda + API Gateway, Amplify, S3, DynamoDB, Bedrock Knowledge Base, CloudFront, WAF, Cognito, SSM Parameter Store → deliverable: live system publicly accessible on AWS. Phase 4 — Monitoring & optimization (Weeks 9–10): CloudWatch, Alarm → SNS, EventBridge cron, cost optimization → deliverable: active monitoring dashboard + alerting pipeline. Phase 5 — Testing & documentation (Weeks 11–12): end-to-end validation, bilingual workshop, clean-up guide → deliverable: workshop website + final internship report. 6. Budget Estimation Infrastructure Costs
AWS Services: AWS Lambda: ~$0/month (within free tier 1M requests/month, 512 MB memory). Amazon Bedrock (Claude 3.5 Sonnet + Titan Embeddings V2): ~$2–3/month (~1,000–1,500 IaC audit requests, pay-per-token). API Gateway (HTTP API): ~$1/month ($1/million requests). AWS Amplify: ~$1/month (build minutes + Next.js SSR hosting). Amazon S3: ~$0.05/month (storing Terraform templates, CIS rules, and compiled PDF reports). Amazon DynamoDB: ~$0.50/month (audit session history and compliance scores, On-Demand mode). Amazon SES: ~$0.10 per 1,000 emails (scheduled audit summaries and alerts). AWS WAF: ~$6/month (Web ACL attached at CloudFront edge + managed rule sets). CloudFront CDN: ~$1–2/month (static assets/SSR distribution and global API caching). CloudWatch + SNS + EventBridge: ~$0–1/month (centralized logging, critical alerts, and daily cron triggers). SSM Parameter Store: ~$0/month (standard parameters are free). Total: ~$11–15/month
Cost-saving architecture choice: The platform leverages 100% serverless compute and Bedrock On-Demand pricing rather than provisioning dedicated EC2/GPU instances (saving $100–$200/month). It eliminates the NAT Gateway (~$32/month) by connecting Lambda directly to internal AWS service endpoints over TLS, keeping total idle operating costs at $0.
7. Risk Assessment Risk Matrix
LLM Hallucination: high severity. Bedrock Model Quota / Rate Limiting: medium severity. Sensitive credential leakage (AWS Keys, API Tokens, PII) in uploaded code: high severity. Lambda cold-start latency: low severity. Unexpected billing beyond free tier: low severity. Mitigation Strategies
Hallucination: Anchor retrieval to CIS Benchmark v3.0 via RAG, set temperature = 0.1 for deterministic scoring, mandate explicit rule citation. Rate limiting: Implement exponential backoff retry in Lambda; cache audit results for identical code hashes in DynamoDB. Sensitive data protection: Activate Bedrock Guardrails to automatically detect and redact secrets, credentials, and PII prior to model invocation. Cost control: Configure AWS Budgets and CloudWatch Billing Alarms at a $5/month threshold; tear down resources post-demo. Credentials: Store all secrets in SSM Parameter Store; git-ignore .env; rotate IAM keys periodically. Contingency Plans
If Claude 3.5 Sonnet experiences regional service throttling, failover dynamically to Claude 3 Haiku via SSM configuration. Local regex-based fallback scanner for foundational rules (port 22, port 3389) during AI network degradation. Complete clean-up guide ensures immediate teardown of all provisioned cloud resources post-presentation to halt all costs. 8. Expected Outcomes Technical Improvements: The entire platform operates serverless on AWS — auto-scaling with traffic, HTTPS-only, WAF and Cognito protected, executing AI and RAG compliance analysis in under 10 seconds. Automated code remediation with CloudWatch monitoring and SNS alerting replaces manual reviews. Long-term Value: A production-grade reference architecture for enterprise GenAI & RAG DevSecOps on AWS, a reusable bilingual step-by-step workshop for the cloud community, and a cost-optimized model (~$11–15/month) validated against real-world infrastructure code.

title: Building RAG Knowledge Base with CIS Benchmark
content:
5.3 Building RAG Knowledge Base with CIS Benchmark The foundational breakthrough of CloudGuard AI over traditional regex-based static scanners lies in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Instead of permitting the LLM to hallucinate rules based on generic pre-training, we anchor its reasoning directly to the authoritative industry benchmark: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0.
In this hands-on section, you will format benchmark rules, upload them to Amazon S3, and provision an Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base vector-indexed by Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2.
Step 1: Prepare the Structured CIS Benchmark Dataset We construct a clean, semantically structured text file containing critical regulatory rules from the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0.
Create cis_v3_benchmark_rules.txt in your local directory or CloudShell: # CIS AWS FOUNDATIONS BENCHMARK V3.0 SECURITY SPECIFICATIONS ## SECTION 1: IDENTITY AND ACCESS MANAGEMENT (IAM) ### RULE CIS-1.16: Ensure IAM Policies Do Not Permit Full Administrative Privileges (*) - Severity: CRITICAL - Impact: Grants unauthorized entity total control over AWS infrastructure. - Recommendation: Restrict permissions to specific actions and resources required for job duties. Avoid "Action": "*" and "Resource": "*". - Terraform Fix Pattern: Avoid: Statement = [{ Action = "*", Resource = "*", Effect = "Allow" }] Enforce: Statement = [{ Action = ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject"], Resource = "arn:aws:s3:::specific-bucket/*", Effect = "Allow" }] ## SECTION 2: STORAGE & AMAZON S3 ### RULE CIS-2.1.1: Ensure S3 Bucket Has Default Encryption Enabled - Severity: HIGH - Impact: Unencrypted stored objects are susceptible to data exfiltration and compliance failure (HIPAA, PCI-DSS). - Recommendation: Configure server-side encryption with SSE-S3 (AES256) or AWS KMS customer-managed keys (aws:kms). - Terraform Fix Pattern: resource "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration" "good" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.target.id rule { apply_server_side_encryption_by_default { sse_algorithm = "AES256" } } } ### RULE CIS-2.1.2: Ensure S3 Bucket Has Public Access Block Configured - Severity: CRITICAL - Impact: Public buckets lead to catastrophic data leaks over the public internet. - Recommendation: Enable block_public_acls, block_public_policy, ignore_public_acls, and restrict_public_buckets. - Terraform Fix Pattern: resource "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block" "good" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.target.id block_public_acls = true block_public_policy = true ignore_public_acls = true restrict_public_buckets = true } ## SECTION 4: NETWORKING & SECURITY GROUPS ### RULE CIS-4.1: Ensure No Security Group Allows Unrestricted Ingress to Port 22 (SSH) - Severity: CRITICAL - Impact: Exposing SSH port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 allows brute-force attacks and unauthorized server takeover. - Recommendation: Restrict port 22 access strictly to designated corporate VPN IP ranges (/32 or /24) or utilize AWS Systems Manager Session Manager (SSM) without open inbound ports. - Terraform Fix Pattern: Avoid: cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] Enforce: cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/16"] # Internal VPC or VPN gateway only ### RULE CIS-4.2: Ensure No Security Group Allows Unrestricted Ingress to Port 3389 (RDP) - Severity: CRITICAL - Impact: Exposing Windows RDP port 3389 to public CIDR ranges exposes workloads to ransomware and credential compromise. - Recommendation: Restrict port 3389 inbound access to corporate bastion hosts or VPN CIDRs. ### RULE CIS-4.3: Ensure Database Ports (3306 MySQL, 5432 PostgreSQL) Are Not Open to 0.0.0.0/0 - Severity: HIGH - Impact: Direct public internet exposure of databases enables automated injection and credential stuffing attacks. - Recommendation: Database security groups must only accept traffic from application layer security groups. Confirm the line count of the created file: wc -l cis_v3_benchmark_rules.txt Step 2: Upload Dataset to Amazon S3 Sync the rules file into the knowledge-base/ prefix in the S3 bucket created previously:
aws s3 cp cis_v3_benchmark_rules.txt s3://cloudguard-audit-data-${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}/knowledge-base/ Verify successful upload:
aws s3 ls s3://cloudguard-audit-data-${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}/knowledge-base/ Step 3: Create Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base We now bind the S3 source into a Bedrock Knowledge Base:
Open the AWS Management Console and navigate to Amazon Bedrock. In the left navigation bar, choose Knowledge bases (under Builder tools). Click Create knowledge base. Step 1 - Provide knowledge base details: Knowledge base name: Enter CloudGuard-CIS-KnowledgeBase. Description: Authoritative repository of CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0 rules for automated IaC security audits. IAM Permissions: Select Create and use a new service role. Click Next. Step 2 - Configure data source: Data source name: cis-benchmark-s3-source. S3 URI: Click Browse S3 and select s3://cloudguard-audit-data-[account-id]/knowledge-base/. Leave chunking strategies at Default chunking (300 tokens, 20% overlap). Click Next. Step 3 - Select embeddings model and configure vector store: Embeddings model: Choose Titan Text Embeddings V2 (amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0) with 1,024 dimensions. Vector database: Select Quick create a new vector store (Amazon Bedrock automatically orchestrates an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless vector collection). Click Next. Step 4 - Review and create: Review all specifications and click Create knowledge base. OpenSearch Serverless collection provisioning takes approximately 3-5 minutes. Step 4: Synchronize Data Source (Data Ingestion) Once the Knowledge Base status transitions to active:
Scroll down to the Data source table. Select cis-benchmark-s3-source. Click the Sync button. The ingestion pipeline reads cis_v3_benchmark_rules.txt, applies chunking, invokes Titan Text Embeddings V2 to generate mathematical vectors, and indexes them into OpenSearch Serverless. In 1-2 minutes, the status updates to green: Complete. Copy the Knowledge Base ID (e.g., AB1CDE2FGH) shown under the knowledge base header; this identifier is required for the Lambda function configuration in the next step!
Step 5: Test Semantic Retrieval in the Bedrock Console Amazon Bedrock provides a built-in interactive Test knowledge base panel:
On the right test drawer, under Select model, choose Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Enter the test prompt: “What is the CIS Benchmark severity and Terraform remediation for Security Group SSH port 22 open to 0.0.0.0/0?”
Click Run. Observe the synthesized answer: Identifies rule CIS-4.1 with CRITICAL severity. Provides clean remediated code (cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/16"]). Click on Citations to verify that the answer references the exact chunk extracted from cis_v3_benchmark_rules.txt. Our RAG system is verified and production-ready. Next, we build the AWS Lambda Core Audit Engine to expose this intelligence over an automated API!

title: Deploying Dashboard & Automated Scheduler
content:
5.5 Deploying Dashboard & Automated Scheduler An enterprise security platform cannot remain confined to terminal command lines. To empower DevOps engineers and security stakeholders, CloudGuard AI provides:
An interactive Web Dashboard (built on React / Next.js and deployed via AWS Amplify). A Serverless Scheduled Automation system using Amazon EventBridge Scheduler for hands-free daily posture reviews. An emergency alerting pipeline powered by Amazon SNS dispatching alerts when CRITICAL severity vulnerabilities are discovered. Step 1: Web Dashboard Architecture The CloudGuard AI interface is designed with a modern, high-contrast, security-focused aesthetic:
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | 🛡️ CloudGuard AI - DevSecOps & FinOps Posture Dashboard | +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | [ Paste Terraform Code Here ] | | resource "aws_security_group" "web" { ... } | | | | [ ⚡ Run Security & Cost Audit Now ] | +-----------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+ | 📊 COMPLIANCE SCORE: | 🚨 DETECTED VIOLATIONS (2): | | [ 45 / 100 ] (POOR - CRITICAL) | • CIS-4.1 [CRITICAL] SSH Port 22 Open | | | • CIS-2.1.1 [HIGH] S3 Unencrypted | +-----------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+ | ✨ REMEDIATED CODE (READY TO DEPLOY): | | resource "aws_security_group" "web" { | | cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/16"] # Fixed by Claude 3.5 Sonnet | | } | | [ 📋 Copy Remediated Code ] | +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ Core UI Components: Code Editor Input: Clean input area for pasting main.tf, security.tf, and iam.tf templates. Security Gauge Visualizer: Calibrated posture score wheel: Red (0 - 49): Unacceptable risk posture, immediate blocker for deployment. Amber (50 - 79): Moderate risks present, remediation recommended before production merge. Green (80 - 100): Compliant with CIS Benchmark standards, approved for release. Findings Accordion: Granular issue breakdown tagged with severity badges (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW), linking specific offending lines to governing CIS clauses. Auto-Remediation Diff Viewer: Displays clean, syntactically valid remediated Terraform code with a single-click copy action. Step 2: Configure Recurring Scans via Amazon EventBridge Scheduler To ensure running infrastructure does not drift into an insecure state, we configure Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to invoke our Lambda engine at 1:00 AM daily.
Create the trust policy granting EventBridge Scheduler execution permissions (scheduler-trust-policy.json): { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "Service": "scheduler.amazonaws.com" }, "Action": "sts:AssumeRole" } ] } Create the IAM Role CloudGuard_Scheduler_Role: aws iam create-role \ --role-name CloudGuard_Scheduler_Role \ --assume-role-policy-document file://scheduler-trust-policy.json Attach the inline invocation policy: aws iam put-role-policy \ --role-name CloudGuard_Scheduler_Role \ --policy-name InvokeLambdaPolicy \ --policy-document "{ \"Version\": \"2012-10-17\", \"Statement\": [ { \"Effect\": \"Allow\", \"Action\": \"lambda:InvokeFunction\", \"Resource\": \"${LAMBDA_ARN}\" } ] }" Create the recurring schedule: aws scheduler create-schedule \ --name "CloudGuard-DailyPosturedAudit" \ --schedule-expression "cron(0 1 * * ? *)" \ --flexible-time-window '{"Mode": "OFF"}' \ --target "{ \"Arn\": \"${LAMBDA_ARN}\", \"RoleArn\": \"arn:aws:iam::${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}:role/CloudGuard_Scheduler_Role\", \"Input\": \"{\\\"terraform_code\\\": \\\"resource \\\\\"aws_security_group\\\\\" \\\\\"default\\\\\" { ingress { from_port = 22 to_port = 22 protocol = \\\\\"tcp\\\\\" cidr_blocks = [\\\\\"0.0.0.0/0\\\\\"] } }\\\"}\" }" \ --region ${AWS_REGION} Verify schedule creation:
aws scheduler get-schedule --name "CloudGuard-DailyPosturedAudit" --region ${AWS_REGION} Step 3: Configure Amazon SNS for Real-Time Escalation When lethal misconfigurations are identified (unrestricted database ports, wildcard IAM permissions), the system broadcasts urgent notifications via Amazon SNS.
Create the SNS topic: SNS_TOPIC_ARN=$(aws sns create-topic \ --name cloudguard-critical-alerts \ --query "TopicArn" \ --output text \ --region ${AWS_REGION}) echo "SNS Topic ARN: ${SNS_TOPIC_ARN}" Subscribe an administrative email address: aws sns subscribe \ --topic-arn ${SNS_TOPIC_ARN} \ --protocol email \ --notification-endpoint "your-email@example.com" \ --region ${AWS_REGION} (Check your inbox and click the Confirm subscription link).
Update the Lambda logic to publish critical alerts: has_critical = any(f.get('severity') == 'CRITICAL' for f in audit_result.get('findings', [])) if has_critical or audit_result.get('score', 100) < 70: sns_client = boto3.client('sns', region_name=os.environ.get('AWS_REGION', 'ap-southeast-1')) sns_topic_arn = os.environ.get('SNS_TOPIC_ARN') if sns_topic_arn: alert_message = ( f"🚨 [CloudGuard AI ALERT] CRITICAL Misconfiguration Detected!\n" f"Scan ID: {scan_id}\n" f"Posture Score: {audit_result.get('score')}/100\n" f"Summary: {audit_result.get('summary')}\n\n" f"Please review the audit findings immediately on CloudGuard Dashboard." ) sns_client.publish( TopicArn=sns_topic_arn, Subject="[URGENT] CloudGuard Security Violation Detected", Message=alert_message ) Update the Lambda environment variables:
aws lambda update-function-configuration \ --function-name cloudguard-core-audit-engine \ --environment "Variables={KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ID=${KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ID},DYNAMODB_TABLE=CloudGuard_ScanHistory,SNS_TOPIC_ARN=${SNS_TOPIC_ARN},AWS_REGION=${AWS_REGION}}" \ --region ${AWS_REGION} We now possess an integrated ecosystem: Visual Dashboard, Scheduled Cron Audit, and Instantaneous SNS Notification. In the final module, we conduct End-to-End Validation and Execute Clean Resource Teardown!

title: Workshop
content:
Workshop: Building GenAI & RAG Automated AWS Infrastructure Security & Cost Auditor (CloudGuard AI) Workshop Overview Welcome to the comprehensive, hands-on CloudGuard AI workshop – an end-to-end automated cloud infrastructure security and cost optimization platform (DevSecOps & FinOps) powered by Generative AI and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) on Amazon Web Services (AWS).
In modern cloud engineering, adopting Infrastructure as Code (IaC) with Terraform enables teams to deploy architectures at unprecedented speed. However, without automated Shift-Left Security verification, dangerous misconfigurations frequently slip into production environments: unrestricted SSH Port 22 open to the public internet (0.0.0.0/0), unencrypted Amazon S3 storage buckets, and overly permissive wildcard IAM policies (AdministratorAccess).
This workshop provides step-by-step guidance to build an enterprise-grade auditor from scratch: orchestrating Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet & Titan Text Embeddings V2), Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to parse code syntax, cross-reference the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, compute posture scores (0-100), and generate automated code remediation snippets in real time.
Learning Objectives Upon completing this workshop, you will be able to:
Master RAG Architecture on AWS Bedrock: Provision and manage Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, index authoritative CIS Benchmark standards, and embed documents using Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2. Develop a Serverless Core Audit Engine: Write AWS Lambda logic to parse Terraform HCL Abstract Syntax Trees (AST), orchestrate reasoning agents, and calculate security scores. Deploy Secure API Endpoints: Expose high-throughput RESTful HTTP API routes via Amazon API Gateway for seamless integration with external CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI). Implement Event-Driven Automation & Alerting: Configure EventBridge Scheduler for automated daily posture scans and leverage Amazon SNS for real-time alerting on CRITICAL misconfigurations. Optimize Operational Costs (FinOps): Maintain zero idle runtime costs through 100% serverless architecture, remaining well within the AWS Free Tier. Table of Contents 5.1 Workshop Overview & Solution Architecture Problem context, 6-stage data flow lifecycle, and high-level architectural design. 5.2 Prerequisites & IAM Configuration Enabling Bedrock model access, configuring IAM execution roles, S3 buckets, and DynamoDB tables. 5.3 Building RAG Knowledge Base with CIS Benchmark Storing CIS Benchmark v3.0 standards in S3, creating Knowledge Bases, and running vector sync. 5.4 Building Lambda Core Engine & API Gateway Developing Python audit logic, integrating Bedrock retrieve-and-generate APIs, and binding HTTP routes. 5.5 Deploying Dashboard & Automated Scheduler Designing an interactive web UI and setting up EventBridge Scheduler for continuous compliance. 5.6 End-to-End Testing & Resource Cleanup Executing real-world validation scenarios against flawed Terraform scripts and executing clean resource teardown.
